beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Fragmented Future asks what happens when AI changes the useful scale of government.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Small administrations may gain capabilities while larger authorities gain stronger tools of control.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This book compares those possibilities through history, political economy, and competing future scenarios.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks which decisions belong nearby, and which responsibilities must remain shared.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The aim is resilience through alternatives, rather than one prediction about tomorrow's political map.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine a city-region using AI to prepare a new bus route.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Local staff can compare travel needs without building a vast analytical department.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But the same provider might control the planning model, identities, and service access.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Apparent local independence can conceal dependence on an owner somewhere else.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book treats that hidden control as part of the political arrangement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The boundary changes when consequences reach people beyond the city.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Water flowing downstream carries effects that a local vote cannot keep inside.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed federation combines local experiments with shared rights, infrastructure, and obligations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Wealthier regions cannot simply keep their advantages while abandoning the places supporting them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Smaller government therefore earns its place by the problem it can responsibly handle.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That argument leads to practical questions about replaceable services and independent scrutiny.
